### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via compileDataset (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9905b1a4e47b580bb9d695444a7ee8b0704a4703` — the merge of head `43db93dfabc5a2e6da08abb884644d2c69a01263` into base `9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9905b1a4e47b580bb9d695444a7ee8b0704a4703 && git checkout 9905b1a4e47b580bb9d695444a7ee8b0704a4703
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b 43db93dfabc5a2e6da08abb884644d2c69a01263 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b && git merge --no-ff 43db93dfabc5a2e6da08abb884644d2c69a01263

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0dd6d595fb2cb44ab445a1504d331d6c2cbfb59c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/aggregate-nontemporal-measure-refusal.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/preview-date-bucket-type.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.dataset-writes.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-formula-dimension-authoring.dogfood.test.ts` + cited on `main`: `dataset-compiler.ts` (`compileDataset`'s dimension loop, `assertDeclared`, `assertAggregateFieldTypeCompatible` and `REMEDY_BY_SOURCE_CLASS`, the `declaredValueShape` hook); `validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts` (the dataset leg's four skips, `resolveCubeColumn`, `columnOf`, `shapeOf`, `declarerOf`, `groupKeyClassOf`); `authoring-rules.ts` (the `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates` registry entry, `tier: gating`, `commands: ALL`, `runtimeTypes: ['dataset']`); `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` (`isVirtualSearchField`); `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.dataset-measure-aggregate-field-type-refused.ts`; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`breakingDeclaration`, the five dispositions); `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`; `scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs`; the repo's merge settings; `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/services/service-analytics/CHANGELOG.md` for the sibling precedents; `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`; `.changeset/30773-dataset-dimension-formula-refused.md` as the ② input.

Inputs read: card #30773 body and its three comments (triage 6675591690, seat claim 6676304413, os-dev-report 6677212943); #24426 body and its PR #24505's file list; the dispatch order and the dev's PR body, report, gates and reconcile files on the project mount; PR #30815 body, 10-file list, commit list with trailers, and the net diff vs `main` (merge-base `172eebb2`, 5 ahead, main 6 ahead touching none of the 10 paths); the docs-drift comment 6677216592; the check-runs on this head, read twice; records 6674767869 and 6674911226 on PR #30768 (the query-time sibling).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The predicate is the spec's.** `assertDimensionFieldStored` asks `declaredValueShape(objectName, field)?.type` and judges it with `isVirtualSearchField({ type })`; the lint's two legs judge `shape` and `column.shape` with the same function. No local type list anywhere in the diff; the lint sweep pins every `FieldType.options` entry against `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` with floors on both sides. TRUE.
- **The refusal is located.** Compile: `[dataset-compiler] dataset "X" dimension "Y" (dimensions.N) groups by field "F", which object "O" declares as formula — ... Denormalise the value onto "O" (a stored field, written when the source changes) and point the dimension at that field.`, `DATASET_INVALID` / 400, the voice of the measure gate beside it (`dataset "X" measure "M" applies aggregate ... which object "O" declares as ...`) and the remedy of the query-time doors. Lint: `where` names the dataset or cube and the dimension, `path` is `datasets[N].dimensions[M].field` or `analyticsCubes[N].dimensions.KEY.sql`, the verdict names the field and its declarer (joined object for a dotted path), the hint names the object to store the value on. Pinned at the runtime dataset write door with the door's rewritten path (`datasets.NAME.dimensions[1].field`) and over HTTP (422 naming the id and `dimensions[1].field`; 400 naming the dimension and the remedy). TRUE.
- **The cube leg resolves without guessing.** It rides `columnOf`, which calls `resolveCubeColumn` (the cube's declared joins walked prefix by prefix, then `resolveFieldPath` on the object graph) and stands down on no verdict, an unjudgeable one, a non-`ok` kind or an untyped leaf; an expression `sql` resolves to nothing and is skipped. The storage axis is judged before `groupKeyClassOf`, as the engine orders its doors, and a formula is never JSON-stored, so the two ids cannot fire on one member. The compile has no cube leg because cubes are registered without a compile (measured (b)), which matches #24426's reach exactly. TRUE.
- **Stored, date and measure-side unchanged.** The compile gate returns before throwing for any non-virtual type; a date dimension with or without `dateGranularity` compiles (pinned); every measure pin in `aggregate-nontemporal-measure-refusal.test.ts` is untouched and the new describe pins that a `count` over the formula compiles and a `sum` keeps `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY`. In the lint, the measure branches are untouched; the dimension branches are the same findings built from a hoisted `site` object (`jsonStoredDimensionFinding(site, ...)`, the four fields identical), so the JSON-stored id's paths and texts are unchanged. The #22161 one-line-verdict and one-line-fix GUARDs now cover three ids. TRUE.
- **Tiering.** The compile stands down with no hook, an unresolved field, or a dotted field (the hook answers for the base object only), the measure gate's three tiers, each pinned; the lint leg and the query-time doors keep the dotted case. The compile refuses at the first formula dimension in declaration order whatever the selection names, and the preview test pins that a query naming only the stored dimension is refused too, which is the cost the changeset's Who-moves bullet states.
- **The fixture rewrite in `preview-date-bucket-type.test.ts` weakens no query-time pin.** The shared `DATASET` declared `calc`, `calc_month` and `calc_s`, so every case went red under the gate; the formula dimensions moved to `FORMULA_DATASET` and `FORMULA_TEXT_DATASET` behind one stored dimension, the #28852 and #28977 cases are byte-unchanged, and the five #29167 / #29304 dataset-face cases now pin the compile refusal `toEqual` across native, ObjectQL and preview. The query-time refusal stays pinned on every face that can still reach it: the engine door (`engine-aggregate-query-shape-door.test.ts`), the native and ObjectQL faces and the dry run on the cube path (`objectql-echo-non-date-bucket.test.ts`, cubes are not compiled), and the delegated face (`fallback-delegate-date-bucket-type.test.ts`), all untouched. One arm is now unreachable rather than unpinned: the draft preview's `assertDatasetGroupTargetsStored` call (both its bucket and plain words) cannot see a bare formula dimension, because `queryDataset` compiles first through the same `sourceFieldMeta`, and its `declaredType` never judged a dotted one. The dev names this; a nit below.
- **The lint id rides the right entry.** The registry key is the function `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates`; its JSON-stored dimension leg (#20890), cube leg (#21082) and duration leg (#25778) already ride it with their own ids, the module docblock says the function keeps its name for that reason, and the `rulesRun` contract the runtime door pins is the function name. A fourth id on the same walk over the same positions (`datasets[].dimensions[]`, `analyticsCubes[].dimensions`) with the same skips is the established shape; a separate rule would re-resolve the same object graph and could drift from the JSON-stored leg's skips. Sound.
- **Accept-set and public face.** One new root export, `DIMENSION_VIRTUAL_FIELD_REFUSED` (a string constant) from `@objectstack/lint`, a published package. The fleet's own spelling for this exact class is settled by precedent: `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown`, `email-template-hole-grammar` (three entries) and `list-view-chart-dataset-foreign-object`, each a new gating rule whose id constant joined the same barrel, all shipped `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; `Clause-②: yes` was used for `groupKeyClassOf` (#23235), a function with behaviour. The changeset names the export and says it adds no accepted input, which is true. No spec file, no `.describe()` text, no error code or status moves.

### ② Semver level

Both carriers read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` through `clause2-line.mjs` (`value: no, arm: narrowing`; `value: narrowed`), one line-initial key each. `narrowed` is right by AGENTS.md step 3: a dataset or cube dimension `field` naming a formula is "a value refused", the precedent class above declares the same. The level follows the kind: `minor` on each package the diff moves, `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/lint`, and no other package moves. The `!` title is on the PR and the changeset's first line; the BREAKING section reads Before (measured on `2d04cd2b`) / Now / Unchanged / Who moves / The remedy; one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, which the gate accepted (`[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing+metadata-protocol-narrowed]`, exit 0 locally per the dev and `Check Changeset` green on this head).

**Ledgers.** `narrowed` moves none here: the authorable-surface and authorable-defaults shards are generated from `packages/spec` schemas by `gen:schema`, and this diff touches no spec file, so `check:authorable-surface` has nothing to project; `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` project the migration registries in memory, and no entry is added. `Spec property liveness` is green. The one ledger question is the ADR-0087 disposition itself, below.

**ADR-0087 disposition.** The `no-migration-prescription` exemption is mechanically honest: no key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, no conversion can rewrite a formula dimension into a stored one, and the changeset carries no FROM-to-TO rewrite. Five sibling gating rules shipped under the same words. Against that, the compile door's own measure-side precedent registered a semantic entry (`dataset-measure-aggregate-field-type-refused`, with `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, `relevantWhen: stack-declares datasets`) for a refusal of a stored dataset shape at this same door, and `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` registered one for a new gating rule; and this change does more than refuse a shape that never worked: a stored dataset carrying a formula dimension compiled on `main` and served its stored dimensions, and after this change the whole dataset is refused until an author hand-migrates it, which the Who-moves bullet says. That hand-migration is what the semantic registry projects into the upgrade guide. Not a must-fix (the gate accepts it, the exemption's letter holds, and the order told the dev to ask the seat before writing an entry), but a should-fix the seat decides before the release that ships this.

Check-runs on `0dd6d595` at the second read (about 05:25Z): 21 `completed/success`, among them `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped` (three), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`; 9 `completed/skipped`; 30 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1 to 8 of 8, `Test UI` 1 to 16 of 16, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`); none failed. The all-green landing precondition is the seat's to read on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. The dev's three out-of-scope notes are read and taken up below: the docs page and the skills row (should-fix follow-ups, not this PR), the pre-empted preview arm (nit), the trailer (no effect).
- **`validating-metadata.mdx`.** Hand-written (not under `references/`), last touched by #30006 for a lint rule, and it documents `dimension-json-stored-field-refused` and the cube leg paragraph by paragraph. The new gating id is absent, so the page is drifted by this change. The dispatch's file surface excluded docs and told the dev to report, which they did, and the refusal text, the hint and `os explain dimension-virtual-field-refused` carry the prescription, so the PR is not held for it; it is owed as a docs-only follow-up PR (a paragraph beside the JSON-stored one and one sentence in the cube paragraph), carrier the seat.
- **`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` line 131** ("virtual: not aggregatable, a dataset measure needs a stored field") could add "nor a group key". Tier H governed surface: a skills seat's follow-up, not this PR; the dev rightly left it. Skills-docs line is honest.
- **WIP commit `098b2b92`** carries a `Claude-Session` trailer naming the coordinator's session; the three later commits carry the dev session's. The repository allows squash merges only (`squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE`, `squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY`), so no branch commit message reaches `main`; the pre-push gate `check-commit-card-trailers.mjs` judges card relations and model identifiers, not session identity; and AGENTS.md forbids rewriting a pushed `claude/project-thread-*` branch. No effect on landing, no action.
- `objectql-strategy.ts` and the engine door are untouched: the query-time refusal of #30768 stands as it landed, and this PR adds the authoring half in front of it.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the PR is a draft; no auto-merge to disarm.
- Independence: rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent fed the card, #24426, the dispatch order, the PR, the net diff, the cited code on `main`, the CHANGELOG precedents, the gate sources and the check-runs, not the seat's conclusions; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing against the spec on `main`: `isVirtualSearchField` declares a formula computed on read with no column; sort, filter, search, value aggregates, buckets and (since #30768) plain groups all refuse it at query time, and the measure side already refuses it at authoring (#24426). A dataset dimension is a group key, so a formula dimension is a declaration no query can serve; refusing it where it is written is Prime Directive 12's contract-first half and takes no working capability away. Holds.
- `dataset-compiler.ts`: the gate sits after `assertDeclared` as the measure gate sits after the join check, so a dotted field is refused for its real fault first; it reads the same hook, stands down the same way, and throws the same error class. Holds against `compileDataset` and every door that compiles through the service's one `compile()`.
- `validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`: one site object per member, the storage axis judged first, the same resolver and skips as the JSON-stored leg, one verdict and one hint under 200 characters with the reasoning in `rule-explanations.ts`. Holds against the registry entry (gating, all three commands, the dataset runtime write) and the #22161 shape.
- The dogfood pin proves the runtime save door (422 with the id and path) and the inline dataset door (400 `DATASET_INVALID`, both selections) on the stock showcase, with controls. Holds.

Findings (none must-fix):

- **should-fix** — for the seat before the release that ships this: decide the ADR-0087 disposition on the record. Either register a semantic entry mirroring `18.dataset-measure-aggregate-field-type-refused` (surface: a dataset or `analyticsCubes` dimension over a virtual field; replacement: a stored field written when the source changes, or the dimension removed; reason and acceptance; `relevantWhen: stack-declares datasets` and `analyticsCubes`), so the upgrade guide carries the hand-migration a stored dataset now needs, in this PR or a spec follow-up before release; or state in the ACCEPT why the lint-rule precedent (`no-migration-prescription`, five entries) governs over the compile-door precedent (`registered`). The marker as written passes the gate either way.
- **should-fix** — docs follow-up, carrier the seat: `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` lists the dataset and cube rules and lacks `dimension-virtual-field-refused`; a paragraph beside `dimension-json-stored-field-refused` and a sentence in the cube paragraph, in a docs-only PR.
- **should-fix** — skills follow-up, carrier a skills seat: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` line 131, "nor a group key" on the formula row (governed, Tier H).
- **nit** — the draft preview's `assertDatasetGroupTargetsStored` arm in `analytics-service.ts` is now unreachable for a bare dataset dimension (the compile precedes it through the same hook) and never judged a dotted one; its pin moved to the compile. Either remove the call or leave a comment saying it is the bucket door's partner only; carrier none.
- **nit** — the compile message's clause "every query selecting this dimension is refused" states the query-time fact, while the error now reaches callers whose selection did not name the dimension; "every query on this dataset" would match what the reader just saw.
- **nit** — the two GUARD-style pins that assert the cube and dataset legs never fire together rely on "a formula is never JSON-stored"; a one-line sweep asserting `groupKeyClassOf` is `null` for every `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` member would pin that premise.
